transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I can’t stay focused on the actual experiment anymore. In a grant call or a safety meeting, I’ll notice a pump vibrating, something a student says, or an odd peak in an old spectrum, and then I’m off following that for hours. Meanwhile the thing everyone actually needs me to do just falls apart.
When did you first start noticing this kind of distractibility and difficulty staying focused—did it begin in childhood, or is this a more recent change in your life?
It’s more recent. It’s been going on about seven months, since I took over the multi-site spectroscopy project.
Over these past seven months, have you noticed a change in your overall mood—such as feeling unusually sad, down, or conversely unusually elevated or irritable—most of the day, nearly every day?

I haven’t felt down. I’ve felt almost electrified, like the lab is finally moving at my speed. But I’ve also been really irritable—if someone questions my plan or tells me to slow down, I snap at them. It’s gotten bad enough that some of the students avoid coming to my office.
During these past seven months, have you noticed you need much less sleep than usual and still feel full of energy the next day?

Yeah. Most nights I only sleep two or three hours—sometimes I just fall asleep on the couch with my laptop open. Then I wake up feeling sharp and ready to work, not tired at all. Sleep just feels like an inefficient interruption.

Have you ever had a period in the past—lasting days or weeks—where you felt unusually depressed, low-energy, or hopeless, or conversely, an earlier episode of feeling this same kind of high energy and reduced need for sleep?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of a clear earlier period like this, or a time when I was depressed or hopeless.

Has this period of high energy and reduced sleep caused serious problems—for example, conflicts at work, risky decisions, spending sprees, or any safety concerns—that have significantly disrupted your daily functioning?

Yes. My department has had to take over decisions I normally handle. I was missing priorities, getting the schedule confused, and the way I was supervising people was causing problems. They were worried it could affect the project and the lab’s safety expectations.
